# Assess distress and manage formal restructuring

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

A specialist-reviewed distress decision and authorized restructuring or insolvency handoff with actions, receipts and outstanding duties tracked.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source checked on 2026-11-01. No case-specific legal review, independent professional assurance or completed execution is claimed. Sources establish regional entry points; determine the actual applicable local route with qualified reviewers.

An agent can prepare and reconcile the documented inputs. Named people retain decisions, specialist judgments, physical work and authorized external actions.

## Outcomes

- A specialist-reviewed distress decision and authorized restructuring or insolvency handoff with actions, receipts and outstanding duties tracked.

| Information to gather | Required by the record |

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Assemble an urgent financial and creditor record

agent-runnable


Prepare current cash, liabilities, overdue amounts, asset records, forecasts, security interests, guarantees and creditor notices in the private case file. Flag imminent hearings, demands or payment failures immediately to the accountable directors and adviser.

- Sources: [GOV.UK closing a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/closing-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Obtain the specialist distress assessment

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The directors obtain qualified local insolvency and legal advice on the actual financial position, duties and available routes. This guide does not determine solvency or authorize continued trading, asset transfers, distributions or a solvent strike-off route.

- Sources: [GOV.UK closing a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/closing-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare the reviewed options and action timetable

agent-runnable


Under adviser instructions, prepare the options, cash and creditor schedules, required decision records and proposed communication plan. Keep operational continuity, employee issues, secured claims and disputed liabilities visible; do not infer that a proposed rescue has legal effect.

- Sources: [GOV.UK closing a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/closing-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve the specific restructuring or insolvency route

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The authorized decision-makers approve the adviser-reviewed route and any required appointments, applications or communications. Keep named authority and specialist review for each consequential action; unresolved duties or deadlines require urgent escalation.

- Sources: [GOV.UK closing a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/closing-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Hand off and carry out authorized formal actions

human · human approval required · hard to undo


The appointed practitioner, lawyer or authorized person completes the approved notices, applications and appointments through the applicable route. Record the responsible operator and retain formal acceptance and case references; an internal plan does not start a formal procedure.

- Sources: [GOV.UK closing a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/closing-a-limited-company)

<a id="step-6"></a>

### 6. Track formal milestones and continuing duties

agent-runnable


Reconcile the adviser handoff, formal case records and approved communications. Maintain a dated action register for required reports, payments and continuing duties, and obtain the specialist completion or closure evidence before closing the case.

- Verify: A specialist-reviewed distress decision and authorized restructuring or insolvency handoff with actions, receipts and outstanding duties tracked.
- Sources: [GOV.UK closing a limited company](https://www.gov.uk/closing-a-limited-company)
